To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hMSCs from four different donors can be cultured and detached from two different types of microcarriers using four different enzymes in three different bioreactors.
the detachment of hMSC from microcarriers is possible at N JS in a variety of bioreactors and that the cells retain their quality attributes.
the agitation strategy of short periods of intense agitation is a scaleable method for the culture and harvest of hMSCs on microcarriers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a robust process to grow hMSCs in microcarrier bioreactors.

the development of a scaleable and robust protocol for the expansion of hMSCs on microcarriers in a variety of bioreactor platforms and their detachment from the microcarriers for further downstream processing.
the development of an industrial process for the large-scale production of hMSCs for use in cell-based therapies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the agitation conditions for hMSCs culture and detachment from microcarri-ers can be scaled up and down without the use of any specific scaleable protocol.

hMSCs can be cultured in a wide range of different bioreactor platforms using a simple agitation strategy and that the detachment of cells from microcarriers can be achieved in-situ in these platforms without the need for a separate harvest step.
for hMSCs, the agitation conditions for culture and harvest can be the same.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the agitation conditions for culture and detachment can be optimized to minimize the risk of cell damage and hence the loss of cell quality attributes.

hMSCs can be cultured and detached from microcarriers at the lowest possible agitation speeds, N JS, in multiple bioreactors, and that this approach can be used for a range of microcarriers, enzymes, growth media, and donor cells.
we have been able to successfully scale-up the culture of hMSCs using a simple agitation strategy and the detachment of these cells in-situ in multiple bioreactors up-to 2.5 L scale.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of the minimum speed of agitation required for complete microcarriers suspension, N JS, is a sound basis for both culture and detachment in a range of scales of bioreactor platforms, from 15mL to 2.4L.
hMSCs are very robust and can be cultured and detached from microcarriers with minimal impact on their quality attributes.
the agitation conditions for culture and detachment are different, but both can be achieved with minimal agitation and the cells can be harvested with minimal damage.
